question:
Choose the most appropriate one-word substitution for “A paper written in one’s own handwriting”


(Junior Secretariat Assistant)
options: Manuscript
Transcript
Parchment
Scroll
solution:
The Correct Answer is: Manuscript

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Manuscript – हस्तलिपि – A document written by hand, especially an author's original copy before printing.
Example: "The museum displayed an ancient manuscript of the poet's unpublished works."

Transcript – प्रतिलिपि – A written or printed version of material originally presented in another medium.
Example: "She requested a transcript of the court proceedings."

Parchment – चर्मपत्र – A stiff, flat material made from the prepared skin of an animal, used historically for writing.
Example: "The royal decree was inscribed on a piece of parchment."

Scroll – पुस्तक का लपेटा हुआ भाग – A roll of parchment, paper, or other material used for writing or painting.
Example: "The ancient scroll contained sacred texts."

Conclusion:
"Manuscript" is the best one-word substitute because it specifically refers to a document written in one's own handwriting, distinguishing it from printed or copied materials. The other options refer to different forms of written or historical documents but do not emphasize the handwritten aspect.

loam
clay
lava

Example: "The lava from the volcano destroyed several homes."

dirt – मिट्टी/गंदगी – Loose soil or earth; also refers to unclean matter.

Example: "She molded the clay into a beautiful vase."

Conclusion:
"Lava" is the correct one-word substitute because it specifically refers to molten rock ejected from a volcano, which matches the underlined phrase. The other options refer to types of soil or earth and do not fit the context.

question:
Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given words.The state of being married to one person at a time
(TCS)
options: Polygamy
Homogamy
Bigamy
Monogamy
solution:
The Correct Answer is: Monogamy

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Monogamy – एकपत्नीत्व – The state or practice of being married to one person at a time.
Example: "Many cultures practice monogamy as the standard form of marriage."

Polygamy – बहुपत्नीत्व – The practice or custom of having more than one wife or husband at the same time.
Example: "Polygamy is legally permitted in some countries."

Homogamy – समान विवाह – Marriage between individuals who are similar in certain characteristics, such as social status or ethnicity.
Example: "Homogamy is common in societies where people prefer partners from similar backgrounds."

Bigamy – द्विविवाह – The offense of marrying someone while already married to another person.
Example: "Bigamy is considered a crime in many legal systems."

Conclusion:
"Monogamy" is the correct one-word substitute as it specifically refers to the state of being married to one person at a time, which matches the given definition. The other options either refer to multiple marriages or unrelated concepts.

question:

Example: "The philanthropist donated millions to charity."

Conclusion:
"Misanthropist" is the correct one-word substitute as it specifically refers to someone who dislikes and avoids other people, unlike the other options which do not convey the same meaning.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A film shown during the day, especially in the afternoon
(SICPO Paper I 2024)
options: Theatre
Cinema
Dramatics
Matinee
solution:
The Correct Answer is: Matinee

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Matinee – [मैटिनी] – [A performance or showing of a movie or play held in the daytime, especially in the afternoon.]
Example: "We decided to watch the matinee show of the new movie to avoid the evening crowd."

Theatre – [थिएटर] – [A building or outdoor area where plays, movies, or other performances are presented.]
Example: "The theatre was packed for the opening night of the play."

Dramatics – [नाटकीय कला] – [The art or practice of acting and staging plays; exaggerated emotional behavior.]
Example: "She studied dramatics in college and later became a successful actress."

Cinema – [सिनेमा] – [A theater where movies are shown; the production and showing of films as an art or industry.]
Example: "The new cinema in town has state-of-the-art sound systems."

Conclusion:
"Matinee" is the correct one-word substitute because it specifically refers to a daytime showing of a film or performance, especially in the afternoon. The other options refer to broader concepts like theaters, acting, or the film industry, but do not denote the specific timing of the show.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who is excessively concerned with their own appearance
(Constable)
options: Introvert
Narcissist
Misanthrope
Extrovert
solution:
The Correct Answer is: Narcissist

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Narcissist – आत्ममुग्ध व्यक्ति – A person who has an excessive interest in or admiration of themselves, particularly their physical appearance.
Example: "He was such a narcissist that he spent hours taking selfies every day."

Introvert – अंतर्मुखी – A person who is predominantly concerned with their own thoughts and feelings rather than external things.
Example: "Being an introvert, she preferred reading books alone over attending parties."

Misanthrope – मानवद्वेषी – A person who dislikes humankind and avoids human society.
Example: "The old man was a misanthrope who rarely spoke to his neighbors."

Extrovert – बहिर्मुखी – An outgoing, socially confident person.
Example: "As an extrovert, he loved being the center of attention at gatherings."

Conclusion:
"Narcissist" is the correct one-word substitute because it specifically refers to someone excessively preoccupied with their own appearance, unlike the other options which describe different personality traits.

question:

Conclusion:
"Laudable" is the best one-word substitute because it specifically means deserving praise or admiration, even if the outcome is not entirely successful, which matches the given phrase perfectly. The other options do not convey the same meaning.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A place where dead bodies are kept for identification

(MTS Non technical and Havaldar Examination 2021)
options: Hutch
Tannery
Crematorium
Morgue
solution:
The Correct Answer is: Morgue

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Morgue – शवगृह – A place where dead bodies are kept temporarily for identification or autopsy.
Example: "The police took the unidentified body to the morgue for further examination."

Hutch – खरगोश का बाड़ा – A cage or pen for small animals, especially rabbits.
Example: "The rabbit was kept in a wooden hutch in the backyard."

Crematorium – श्मशान – A place where dead bodies are cremated.
Example: "The funeral procession ended at the crematorium."

Tannery – चमड़ा कारखाना – A place where animal hides are processed into leather.
Example: "The foul smell near the river was coming from the tannery."

Conclusion:
"Morgue" is the correct one-word substitute as it specifically refers to a place where dead bodies are stored temporarily, unlike the other options which relate to animal enclosures, cremation, or leather processing.

question:

Free time; time at one’s own disposal
(CHSL Exam 2023 Tier I)
options: Legible
Legion
Lethal
Leisure
solution:
The Correct Answer is: Leisure

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Leisure – फुरसत – Time free from work or duties when one can relax or engage in enjoyable activities.
Example: "She enjoys reading books in her leisure time."

Lethal – घातक – Capable of causing death.
Example: "The snake's venom is lethal to humans."

Legible – स्पष्ट पढ़ने योग्य – Clear enough to read.
Example: "Her handwriting is neat and legible."

Legion – बड़ी संख्या – A large number of people or things.
Example: "He has a legion of fans across the world."

Conclusion:
"Leisure" is the correct one-word substitute for "free time; time at one’s own disposal" because it specifically refers to periods when one is not occupied with work or responsibilities and can relax or pursue hobbies. The other options do not relate to the given phrase.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Government by king or queen

(MTS Non technical and Havaldar Examination 2021)
options: Plutocracy
Capitalism
Oligarchy
Monarchy
solution:
The Correct Answer is: Monarchy

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Monarchy – राजतंत्र – A form of government with a monarch (king or queen) at the head.
Example: "The United Kingdom is a constitutional monarchy where the king or queen has limited powers."

Oligarchy – अल्पतंत्र – A government ruled by a small group of powerful people.
Example: "Some ancient Greek city-states were governed as oligarchies."

Capitalism – पूंजीवाद – An economic system where trade and industry are controlled by private owners for profit.
Example: "The United States follows a capitalist economic model."

Plutocracy – धनिकतंत्र – A government controlled by the wealthy.
Example: "Critics argue that some modern democracies are turning into plutocracies due to corporate influence."

Conclusion:
"Monarchy" is the correct one-word substitute for a system of government ruled by a single sovereign, such as a king or queen, while the other options refer to different forms of governance or economic systems.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Any female animal which feeds its young on milk from her own body
(Combined Graduate Level Examination Tier I 2023)
options: Fauna
Mammal
Parasite
Vertebrate
solution:
The Correct Answer is: Mammal

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Mammal – स्तनधारी – A warm-blooded vertebrate animal of a class that is distinguished by the possession of hair or fur, the secretion of milk by females for the nourishment of the young, and (typically) the birth of live young.
Example: "Humans, dogs, and whales are all examples of mammals."

Fauna – जीवजंतु – The animals of a particular region, habitat, or geological period.
Example: "The fauna of the Amazon rainforest is incredibly diverse."

Parasite – परजीवी – An organism that lives in or on another organism (its host) and benefits by deriving nutrients at the host's expense.
Example: "Ticks are parasites that feed on the blood of mammals."

Vertebrate – कशेरुकी – An animal of a large group distinguished by the possession of a backbone or spinal column, including mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fishes.
Example: "Fish, birds, and humans are all vertebrates."

Conclusion:
"Mammal" is the correct one-word substitute because it specifically refers to female animals that feed their young with milk from their own bodies, which is a defining characteristic of mammals. The other options do not accurately describe this trait.

Conclusion:
"Nephrologist" is the correct one-word substitute because it specifically refers to a doctor who specializes in kidney diseases, unlike the other options which pertain to different medical specialties.

solution:
The Correct Answer is: Oligarchy

Oligarchy – अल्पतंत्र – A form of government where power is held by a small group of people.
Example: "The country was ruled by an oligarchy of wealthy elites."

Plutocracy – धनिकतंत्र – A government controlled by the wealthy.
Example: "Critics argue that the nation has become a plutocracy, where policies favor the rich."

Democracy – लोकतंत्र – A system of government by the whole population, typically through elected representatives.
Example: "India is the world's largest democracy."

Autocracy – एकतंत्र – A system of government where one person has absolute power.
Example: "The king ruled the country as an autocracy, with no checks on his authority."

Conclusion:

Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.

The liberal leadership simply joined the ranks of the existing government by the few.
(SICPO Paper I 2024)
options_hi: Oligarchy
Autocracy
Democracy
Plutocracy
solution_hi:
The Correct Answer is: Oligarchy

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Oligarchy – अल्पतंत्र – A form of government where power is held by a small group of people.
Example: "The country was ruled by an oligarchy of wealthy elites."

Plutocracy – धनिकतंत्र – A government controlled by the wealthy.
Example: "Critics argue that the nation has become a plutocracy, where policies favor the rich."

Democracy – लोकतंत्र – A system of government by the whole population, typically through elected representatives.
Example: "India is the world's largest democracy."

Autocracy – एकतंत्र – A system of government where one person has absolute power.
Example: "The king ruled the country as an autocracy, with no checks on his authority."

Conclusion:
"Oligarchy" is the best one-word substitute for "government by the few" because it specifically refers to rule by a small group, which aligns perfectly with the given phrase. The other options either focus on wealth (plutocracy), the general population (democracy), or a single ruler (autocracy).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who compiles a dictionary
(Combined Graduate Level Examination Tier I 2023)
options: Iconoclast
Plagiarist
Lexicographer
Bibliophile
solution:
The Correct Answer is: Lexicographer

Let's see Explanation of all the options:

Lexicographer – [शब्दकोश संकलनकर्ता] – [A person who compiles dictionaries]
Example: "Samuel Johnson was a famous lexicographer who compiled the first comprehensive English dictionary."

Iconoclast – [मूर्तिभंजक] – [A person who attacks or criticizes cherished beliefs or institutions]
Example: "The artist was considered an iconoclast for challenging traditional art forms."

Plagiarist – [साहित्यिक चोर] – [A person who uses someone else's work and pretends it is their own]
Example: "The author was exposed as a plagiarist after copying entire passages from another book."

Bibliophile – [पुस्तक प्रेमी] – [A person who loves or collects books]
Example: "As a bibliophile, she spent hours browsing through rare books in the library."

Conclusion:
"Lexicographer" is the correct one-word substitute because it specifically refers to a person who compiles dictionaries, whereas the other options describe unrelated roles or traits.
